intro.en: Appointments, common examinations, specialists, sick leave and hospital care: health-system vocabulary for Spain.

nota.en: Seguro médico privado refers specifically to private health insurance.

estar de baja.en: to be on medical sick leave

nota.en: In this lesson, it refers to a period off work for health reasons.

dar el alta.en: to discharge from hospital; to clear someone to return to work

nota.en: The precise meaning depends on the context: alta hospitalaria or the end of medical sick leave.
Antibiotics should only be taken when prescribed by a healthcare professional.
The noun has the same form for a man and a woman: el dentista / la dentista.
The noun has the same form for a man and a woman: el oculista / la oculista.
The noun has the same form for a man and a woman: el paciente / la paciente.
Use ponerse enferma for a woman.
Curar is usually transitive (curar a alguien/una herida); curarse means to recover or heal.
Use mareada for a woman; in the dialogue it means dizzy.

la farmacia de guardia.en: the on-duty pharmacy; the out-of-hours pharmacy

nota.en: A common term in Spain for a pharmacy open outside normal hours.
The profession noun can also be la especialista.
Often used in the plural for emergency care.
Alta is feminine, as in alta médica, but takes el in the singular because the initial a is stressed.
Only fast if your healthcare professional tells you to.

titulo.en: Going to the doctor in Spain

texto.en:
**Primary care in Spain.** You usually contact your local **centro de salud** to request a **cita**; methods vary, and phone or regional online services are common. A **médico/a de cabecera** assesses you and may refer you to **el/la especialista**, such as a **dentista**, **oculista** or **ginecólogo/a**. A private policy may be called **un seguro médico privado**. A routine check-up is often called **una revisión**.

A doctor may request **un análisis de sangre** or give you **una receta**. Follow the instructions for the specific test; the clinician will tell you if you need to come **en ayunas**.

If your health means you cannot work, the doctor can issue **la baja**; you are **de baja**. **Dar el alta** can mean discharging someone from hospital or clearing them to return to work, depending on context.

**In hospital:** **ingresar** means to be admitted; **operar** means to perform surgery.

**Treatment and prevention:** take an antibiotic only if it is prescribed; use drops or cream as directed. **Vacunarse / ponerse una vacuna** is about vaccination and prevention. A **farmacia de guardia** is an on-duty pharmacy in Spain.

To talk about illness and recovery: **ponerse enfermo**, **encontrarse mal**, **mejorar** and **curarse**. If you feel worse, contact the doctor; for an emergency, go to **urgencias**.

frases.es: Buenos días. Quería pedir cita con mi médica.
frases.en: Good morning. I'd like to make an appointment with my doctor.

frases.es: ¿Para cuándo? Mañana a las diez está libre.
frases.en: What day would you like? We have a slot tomorrow at ten.

frases.es: Perfecto. Llevo tres días mareado y no he ido a trabajar.
frases.en: Perfect. I have been dizzy for three days and have not been to work.

frases.es: La médica decidirá si necesita un análisis de sangre y le dirá si hace falta venir en ayunas.
frases.en: The doctor will decide whether you need a blood test and tell you whether to come fasting.
analisis: si necesita un análisis de sangre
si hace falta venir en ayunas

frases.en: And can the doctor put me on sick leave?

frases.es: Eso lo decide la médica. Si se encuentra peor, póngase en contacto con ella; si es una urgencia, vaya a urgencias.
frases.en: That is for the doctor to decide. If you feel worse, contact her; if it is an emergency, go to the emergency department.

**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write an email to ask for a doctor's appointment and explain your symptoms.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Play both parts of a visit to the doctor aloud: appointment, symptoms, tests and treatment.
